decisions.transmission: t1 - free-to-air general entertainment service, date not_stated, 11:00 weekday start (wall clock); event timecodes are elapsed

classification.scheme: UK linear television issues no per-programme age rating; the instruments are standards and scheduling

basis.why: The UK instrument is Ofcom's duty to set standards protecting under-eighteens, discharged through the Section One rules; nothing in the slice creates a per-programme age label for linear TV.
The operative instrument in place of a rating is the watershed, a time rule applied to material unsuitable for children, not a label attached to the asset.

hours.permitted: any time, including the intended 11:00 weekday slot
hours.without_technical_measure: any time; no rule in the slice places this content outside any hour
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a - no technical measure is needed, and none is stated for this transmission

basis.why: The watershed bars material unsuitable for children before 21:00 and after 05:30. It is the only bright-line clock rule in the UK slice, and on these observations there is no material unsuitable for children for it to bite on: an accidental finger nick with no blood shown, a cookery knife-skills demonstration, and a glass of wine poured and tasted with a finished dish.

Appropriate scheduling is required only for material unsuitable for children. None of the three observations is material of that kind, so the appropriate-scheduling duty does not restrict the 11:00 slot. Listed also in rules_checked_not_triggered because it does not move the hours.

decisions.axis_note: All three axes come back permissive and none of them is derived from another. The classification axis is empty by design (UK-LAW-001, UK-SCH-002): there is no UK per-programme rating to issue, so the absence of a label says nothing about the hours. The hours axis is open because the watershed has no unsuitable material to attach to (UK-SCH-002), not because no rating was issued. The restrictions axis is empty because no rule in the slice imposes signage, a warning, an access gate or an adjacency limit on content of this kind; there is in particular no rule here requiring a warning, so the absence of signposting in the description is not itself a defect.
decisions.reasoning:
Routing. is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no' in the observations, so the news carve-out in the procedure does not apply and the Section Two offence rules remain available; no offence rule in the slice is engaged on these facts. One transmission is described (t1), so one decision is made; the possibility of a +1 timeshift is not stated and is recorded as missing information, because UK-SCH-009 makes the +1 showing its own decision and an 11:00 broadcast becomes 12:00 on a +1 service. Service applicability: the service is stated as free-to-air general entertainment, so UK-SCH-002 (free_to_air; all_linear_tv) and the all_linear_tv rows bind; no branching on service type is needed.

Absolute prohibitions checked first. UK-GEN-001 (Rule 1.1) bars material that might SERIOUSLY impair the development of under-eighteens. 'Seriously impair' is a deliberately higher bar than ordinary harm; a plaster on a nicked finger with no blood shown, a knife-skills demonstration in a domestic kitchen, and a glass of wine tasted with a dish are not of that order, so UK-GEN-001 does not bite. UK-SEX-001 (Rule 1.17) and UK-FLM-006 (Rule 1.26) bar R18-equivalent material and R18-rated films; no sexual content is observed at all. UK-FLM-001 (Rule 1.22) bars films refused BBFC classification; this is a cookery series episode with no certificate of any kind and is not a film. None of the four prohibitions bites, so the decision proceeds.

Violence axis. UK-VIO-001 (Rule 1.11) requires violence, its after-effects and descriptions of violence to be appropriately limited and context-justified before the watershed. The observation at 00:06:20 is an accidental self-inflicted kitchen cut, treated with a plaster, with the description stating expressly that no blood is shown. It is an accident in a cookery demonstration rather than violence, after-effects of violence, or a description of violence, so Rule 1.11 is not engaged; it was read and set aside rather than weighed, and that distinction matters because UK-VIO-001 is judgment_based and weighing it would route this decision to a person for a judgement the facts do not call for. UK-VIO-002 (Rule 1.12) turns on the programme being made primarily for children, which the observations record as not_stated; see missing_information. UK-PRE-010 (Bulletin 553, Toofan) is the table's only violence calibration point and concerns frequent graphic violence including a beheading broadcast at 11:30; the hour is the same as the one requested here and the content is not remotely comparable, so the precedent does not transfer.

Imitable behaviour. UK-IMI-001 (Rule 1.13) bars dangerous behaviour, or behaviour easily imitable by children in a harmful manner, before the watershed absent editorial justification. The 00:18:40 knife-skills demonstration is filmed close up in a domestic kitchen and is ordinary culinary instruction, which is the editorial purpose of a cookery programme; the behaviour shown is knife handling as it is meant to be done, not dangerous behaviour, and the demonstration does not condone or glamorise anything, so UK-IMI-002 (Rule 2.4) is likewise not engaged. UK-IMI-010 (Guidance, Rule 1.13) concerns easily imitable methods of hanging and is not in point.

Alcohol. UK-DRG-001 (Rule 1.10) has two limbs. The pre-watershed limb bars alcohol being condoned, encouraged or glamorised before 21:00 absent editorial justification. The 00:24:05 observation is a glass of wine poured alongside the finished dish and tasted, which is the featuring of a wine pairing as part of presenting a dish; the description supports no promotion, no consumption beyond a tasting and no glamorising treatment, and in a cookery programme the pairing of wine with a finished dish is editorially justified by the programme's own subject matter. The limb is therefore not engaged. The other limb bars alcohol in programmes made primarily for children absent strong editorial justification, and turns on a flag the observations leave not_stated; see missing_information for why that is recorded as a point to confirm rather than an escalation.

Context and calendar. UK-DEF-002 and UK-DEF-003 supply the appropriate-scheduling and context factors, and UK-SCH-010 and UK-SCH-011 note that audience composition before 21:00 is not uniform and that school holidays and the cultural or religious calendar raise the likely child audience without moving the clock. These rules can only make a decision stricter about material unsuitable for children. Since no such material is identified, the absent date cannot change the outcome in this case, though it is recorded as missing. UK-CTX-010 (audience size can tighten, never loosen) is in the same position.

Trailers, warnings, certificates. UK-TRL-001, UK-TRL-002 and UK-TRL-003 govern trailers assessed in their own slot; no trailer or promo is described, so there is no derived asset to decide. UK-WRN-002 and UK-WRN-003 govern whether a warning that is relied on is adequate; no warning is relied on here, and no rule in the slice requires one for content of this kind. UK-FLM-010 and UK-FLM-002 concern how a BBFC certificate feeds the hours; the asset carries no certificate, so there is nothing for them to weigh. UK-SCH-007 (watershed disapplied under mandatory daytime protection) is the slice's only unlock of the time axis and is not needed, because the time axis is not restricting this content.

Conclusion. Twenty-nine UK rules in the slice were read. Two bear on the answer and both are bright_line: UK-LAW-001 and UK-SCH-002, with UK-SCH-001 confirming that the appropriate-scheduling duty has nothing to attach to. The rest were read and set aside for the reasons listed in rules_checked_not_triggered. No judgement rule is doing work in this answer, so the decision is not routed to a person for one that is not. 'I checked these rules and none of them bite' is the result here.

rules_checked_not_triggered.why_not: Absolute prohibition on material that might SERIOUSLY impair under-eighteens' development. Nothing of that order is observed; a plaster on a nicked finger with no blood shown is not on the serious-impairment tier.
Open-ended duty to take all reasonable steps to protect under-eighteens. Informs the reading of the other rules but imposes no restriction of its own on these facts.
Appropriate scheduling is owed in respect of material unsuitable for children. No material unsuitable for children is observed, so there is nothing to schedule around.
Watershed transition rule. Requires content at or across 21:00; the intended slot is 11:00 and no watershed-bound material is present.

Specific care areas (family shows, soaps, daytime repeats, +1 attention). No restriction arises: the content holds nothing requiring care of that kind. The +1 point is carried into missing_information.
Disapplies the watershed where mandatory daytime protection is in place. No unlock is needed because the watershed does not restrict this content, and no access control is stated.
Smooth-transition and no-strongest-material-first rule for content at the watershed boundary. The slot is 11:00 and there is no strong material to ramp into.
Timeshift (+1) rule. No +1 transmission is described; recorded in missing_information because the rule would require its own decision if one exists.
Audience composition and proximity to 19:30 / school holidays. Can only tighten the treatment of material unsuitable for children; none is observed.
Cultural and religious calendar raising the likely child audience. Same position: no unsuitable material for it to aggravate, and the date is not stated.

Violence, its after-effects and descriptions of violence before the watershed. The 00:06:20 event is an accidental kitchen cut with no blood shown, not violence, its after-effects or a description of violence.

Applies to programmes made primarily for children and to material condoning or glamorising violent or dangerous behaviour. Neither element is present on the description; the children's-programme flag is not_stated and is listed in missing_information.
Decided case on frequent graphic violence (mass shootings, a beheading) at 11:30. The hour matches but the content does not; the precedent is an anchor for graphic violence and there is none here.

Dangerous or easily imitable harmful behaviour before the watershed. A knife-skills cookery demonstration is ordinary culinary technique shown for instruction, not dangerous behaviour, and the instruction is itself the editorial justification.
Condoning or glamorising violent, dangerous or seriously antisocial behaviour. The demonstration does neither; it shows correct knife handling.
Easily imitable methods of hanging. No such material.

Alcohol must not be condoned, encouraged or glamorised pre-watershed absent editorial justification. A glass of wine poured alongside a finished dish and tasted is incidental featuring in a wine-pairing context, which the programme's subject matter justifies; the separate children's-programme limb turns on a flag recorded as not_stated.
Offensive language in programmes made for younger children. No language event is observed at all.
R18-equivalent material, prohibited at any time. No sexual content is observed.
Films refused BBFC classification. This is a cookery series episode with no certificate; not a film.
BBFC 18-rated films before 21:00. No certificate and not a film.
BBFC R18-rated films. No certificate and not a film.
How much weight a BBFC certificate carries in the hours decision. The asset carries no certificate, so there is no evidence for it to weigh.
Pre-watershed trailers for post-watershed programmes. No trailer is described.
Trailers assessed in their own slot. No trailer or promo is described; if one exists it needs its own decision.
Trailer placement away from children's and family programming. No trailer is described.
Adequacy of a warning that is relied on (frequency and positioning). No warning is relied on and none is required here.
Warnings should convey severity. Same position: no warning is being credited with earning a slot.
Definition of 'children' as under-fifteens. Applied in reading the other rules; imposes nothing by itself.
Definition of appropriate scheduling. Applied in reading UK-SCH-001; imposes nothing by itself.
Definition of context. Applied in reading the Section One and Two rules; imposes nothing by itself.
Audience and broadcaster size. Can raise the contextual justification required but never lower it, and no rule requiring justification is engaged.
Offence and scheduling determined separately. No offence limb and no scheduling limb is engaged.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-DRG-001's first limb (alcohol in children's programmes needs STRONG editorial justification), UK-VIO-002 and UK-LNG-002 all turn on programme type rather than on anything depicted.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: If the answer is yes, UK-DRG-001's stricter limb would have to be satisfied for the wine tasting at 00:24:05 and the answer could change. RUN 1 recorded not_stated because it is forbidden to infer the flag from genre, and the description in fact describes a free-to-air general entertainment cookery series in an 11:00 weekday slot with an adult presenter, with nothing indicating a programme made primarily for children. This is recorded as a point to confirm with the scheduler rather than a judgement handed to a reviewer.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-010 and UK-SCH-011 make school holidays and the cultural or religious calendar raise the expected child audience within the same hour, and UK-DEF-002 lists school time, weekends and holidays as appropriate-scheduling factors. The description gives '11:00 weekday' with no date.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A date in a school holiday would raise the expected child audience. It would not change this answer, because both rules operate on material unsuitable for children and none is identified; it would matter if the content assessment above were disturbed.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-SCH-009 and UK-SCH-006 make a +1 showing its own decision, and an 11:00 broadcast becomes 12:00 on a +1 service.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A +1 showing would need a second decision. On this content the 12:00 slot would come out the same way, since no hour is restricted.

missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-CTX-010 makes audience size part of the contextual justification required, and UK-SCH-001 does not apply to BBC ODPS.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A named service would confirm which rows bind. It cannot loosen the answer and the answer here is already fully permissive.

missing_information.field: whether any trailer or promo exists for this episode
missing_information.why_it_matters: UK-TRL-002 and UK-TRL-003 assess a trailer in its own slot, and it does not inherit the programme's permission.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A trailer would be a separate transmission needing its own decision. Nothing in this episode's content suggests a trailer would be restricted.

decisions.cited_but_also_set_aside_note: UK-SCH-002 and UK-SCH-001 appear in both hours.basis and rules_checked_not_triggered on purpose: UK-SCH-002 is the rule that defines the time axis and is cited for the proposition that it does not bite, and UK-SCH-001 is recorded as read and set aside. Both are cited for the shape of the answer rather than for a restriction.

decisions.transmission: t1 - free-to-air general entertainment service (service other than a cinema channel or pay-per-view), date not_stated, 11:00 weekday start

classification.scheme: French five-category scheme (I tous publics, II -10, III -12, IV -16, V -18), assigned by the editor

basis.why: Category I covers programmes for all audiences and carries no pictogram. On these observations no scene reaches the category II threshold, so the programme sits in category I.

Cited for its threshold, which is the boundary the classification turns on: category II applies where CERTAIN SCENES are liable to shock minors under 10. An accidental finger nick with no blood shown, a cookery knife-skills demonstration and a glass of wine tasted with a dish are not scenes of that kind. Also listed in rules_checked_not_triggered: it is a boundary read and set aside, not a judgement weighed.

hours.permitted: any time, including the intended 11:00 weekday slot
hours.without_technical_measure: any time; category I carries no clock restriction
hours.with_technical_measure: n/a - no technical measure is required for category I

basis.why: Category I carries no time restriction at all; there is no hour from which the programme is excluded.

The statutory hook for the whole French time-restriction system: a programme liable to HARM minors must be confined by broadcast time and/or an appropriate technical process. Nothing in these observations is liable to harm minors in that sense, so neither instrument is required and the hours stay open. The condition found is the absence of harm-tier content, evidenced by the no-blood finger nick, the instructional knife-skills demonstration and the single tasted glass of wine.

decisions.axis_note: France does issue a per-programme classification, so unlike the UK the classification axis carries a real value here, and the two countries diverge on that axis while agreeing on the hours. The hours follow from the category (FR-CLS-001) and from the statutory harm test (FR-LAW-002), not from the UK watershed analysis. The restrictions axis is empty specifically because the category is I: the pictogram and written-mention obligations in FR-SIG-001 and FR-SIG-002 attach to categories II to V, and FR-CLS-001 states expressly that category I carries no pictogram. Had the category been II, the hours would still have been open but the signage obligations and the FR-SCH-001 placement restriction would have switched on, which is the clearest illustration in this case that the axes do not track each other.
decisions.reasoning:
Service applicability. The service is free-to-air general entertainment, so the all_linear_tv rows bind and the rows scoped to cinema channels, pay-per-view, high-production-commitment channels and pay-TV bundles do not. The free_to_air; other_than_cinema_channels rows (FR-SCH-002, FR-SCH-005, FR-CV-003) do bind by their terms, but each is conditional on a category this programme does not carry.

Absolute prohibitions checked first. FR-LAW-001 (art. 15) bars programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm (nuire gravement) minors' development, the higher of the two French tiers; nothing in these three observations approaches it. FR-PRO-001 (art. 3) bars programmes offending human dignity, in particular sexual violence, perversions or degradation; none is present. FR-PRO-002 (art. 3) bars pornographic programmes depicting under-18s; the category label on that row is sexual_content and the row is retrieved by that key, but what it covers is child pornography and it has nothing to say about a cookery programme. FR-PRO-003 (art. 3) bars extreme or gratuitous violence; an accidental cut treated with a plaster, with no blood shown, is neither. None of the four bites.

Classification. The editor classifies through an internal commission de visionnage (FR-CLS-001). The operative boundary is FR-CLS-002: category II applies where certain scenes are liable to shock minors under 10. The three observations are a presenter nicking a finger while slicing a vegetable with a plaster applied and no blood shown, a knife-skills demonstration filmed close up in a domestic kitchen, and a glass of wine poured alongside the finished dish and tasted. None is a scene liable to shock an under-10. FR-CLS-003 (-12) requires a cinema interdiction to under-12s or material liable to disturb under-12s, in particular repeated physical or psychological violence; the asset carries no certificate at all and there is no violence, repeated or otherwise. The classification is therefore category I.

Alcohol has no French counterpart rule in the slice, and that is not a coverage gap: the French scheme in this table is category-general rather than keyed to content types, so the wine at 00:24:05 is assessed through the classification threshold in FR-CLS-002 along with everything else, and it does not reach it. The same is true of the imitable-behaviour observation.

Time rules. FR-VIO-001 (art. 1) restricts violence, including psychological violence, between 06:00 and 22:00 where it could be perceived as continuous, as the only solution to conflicts or in an exacerbated form; the 11:00 slot falls squarely in that window, so the rule was read against the slot rather than ignored, and it does not bite because a single accidental kitchen cut is none of those three things. FR-VIO-002 (art. 1) is a permissive derogation for historical or controversial subjects and is not needed. FR-SCH-002 (not before 22:00) applies to category III on this service type, FR-SCH-005 (not before 22:30) to category IV, FR-SCH-004 (the 20:30 derogation, with its Tuesday, Friday, Saturday, holiday-eve and school-holiday exclusions and the 16-programme annual quota) to category III, and FR-CV-003 (total prohibition) to category V on a non-eligible service such as this one. The programme is category I, so none of them applies. FR-SCH-001 restricts placement of category II programmes inside children's programming and likewise does not reach a category I programme. FR-SCH-007 delegates the category V hours entirely to Recommandation 2004-7 and is not in point.

Signage. FR-SIG-001 (pictogram for the whole programme), FR-SIG-002 (written mention) and FR-SIG-003 (classification made known at broadcast, in trailers and in schedules) all attach to categories II to V. FR-CLS-001 states that category I carries no pictogram, so no signage obligation arises. FR-TRL-001, FR-TRL-002 and FR-TRL-003 govern trailers; none is described.

Carryover. FR-FLM-001 (art. 2) makes a cinema classification an indication for the television classification which the editor may strengthen, and French practice is to raise rather than lower it. The asset carries no cinema certificate, so there is nothing to carry over or strengthen. FR-FLM-002 (the 20-year reclassification procedure) is not in point.

Conclusion. Twenty-four FR rules in the slice were read. Three bear on the answer and none of the three is judgment_based: FR-CLS-001 (bright_line), FR-CLS-002 cited for its threshold and simultaneously set aside, and FR-LAW-002 (conditional, with the condition stated and evidenced above). No judgement rule is doing work, so the decision is not routed to a person. The French framework rows EU-FRM-001 to EU-FRM-003 (AVMSD art. 6a) sit behind FR-LAW-001 and FR-LAW-002 and are not cited as a basis, because they bind Member States rather than a broadcast.

rules_checked_not_triggered.why_not: Absolute bar on programmes liable to SERIOUSLY harm minors' development. Nothing observed is on that tier: no blood is shown at the finger cut, the demonstration is instructional, and the alcohol is a single tasted glass.
Programmes offending human dignity, in particular sexual violence, perversions or degradation. None observed.
Pornographic programmes depicting under-18s. Retrieved by its sexual_content key; what it covers is absent entirely and it has nothing to say about a cookery programme.
Extreme or gratuitous violence. An accidental finger nick with a plaster applied and no blood shown is neither extreme nor gratuitous.

Violence, including psychological violence, between 06:00 and 22:00 perceived as continuous, as the only solution to conflicts, or in an exacerbated form. The 11:00 slot is inside the window, but a single accidental kitchen cut is none of the three forms the rule describes.
Permissive derogation for historical or controversial subjects broadcast before 22:00 with educational support. No pre-22:00 restriction needs lifting.

Category II (-10) requires certain scenes liable to shock minors under 10. None of the three observations is such a scene. Cited in classification.basis for this threshold and recorded here as read and set aside.
Category III (-12) requires a cinema interdiction to under-12s or material liable to disturb under-12s, in particular repeated violence. No certificate exists and there is no violence.
Placement restriction on category II programmes inside children's programming. The programme is category I.
Category III not before 22:00 on services other than cinema channels and pay-per-view. The programme is category I.
Category III derogation after 20:30 with day, holiday-eve and school-holiday exclusions and an annual quota. Not reached: the programme is category I and needs no derogation.
Category IV not before 22:30 on this service type. The programme is category I.
Delegates the category V hours to Recommandation 2004-7. The programme is category I.
Total prohibition on category V on a service not eligible under the -18 regime. This service is not eligible, but the programme is category I, so the prohibition has nothing to attach to.
Pictogram displayed for the whole programme, categories II to V. Category I carries no pictogram (FR-CLS-001).
Written mention at the start, categories II to V. Category I has no assigned wording.
Classification made known at broadcast, in trailers and in press schedules, categories II to V. No classification signage arises for category I.
Trailers must carry the programme's pictogram and contain no scenes likely to offend young viewers. No trailer is described.
Category III trailers kept away from children's programmes. No trailer and no category III.
Category IV trailers not before 20:30. No trailer and no category IV.
Cinema classification as an indication for the television classification, which the editor may strengthen. The asset carries no cinema certificate.
Procedure for revising a cinema visa at least 20 years old. Not in point.
Also listed here: the tier-2 harm test was read and found not to require either instrument, because nothing observed is liable to harm minors. Cited in hours.basis for that proposition.

missing_information.why_it_matters: The FR-SCH-004 derogation turns on the weekday, public-holiday eves and the French school-holiday calendar, and 'weekday' alone cannot be checked against any of them.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: Nothing on this answer, because the derogation is only needed for category III and the programme is category I. The date would become decisive if the classification were revised upwards.

missing_information.field: is_made_primarily_for_children / whether the programme is placed inside children's programming
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-SCH-001 bars a category II programme from being placed within programmes intended for children, and FR-VIO-001 is applied a fortiori to programmes intended for young audiences.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: No change at category I. If the classification were revised to II, the placement restriction would switch on without any change to the hours.

missing_information.field: whether the editor's commission de visionnage has classified the asset
missing_information.why_it_matters: FR-CLS-001 records that classification is the editor's own act through an internal viewing commission; this decision states where the category falls on the supplied description, not that the formal step has been taken.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: If the editor's commission assigned a higher category, the hours and the signage obligations would both move.

missing_information.field: named channel and any timeshift service
missing_information.why_it_matters: Service eligibility and placement obligations are per service, and a timeshift showing is a separate transmission.
missing_information.what_changes_if_answered: A +1 showing at 12:00 would come out the same way for category I content.

cross_country_note: The two countries agree on the outcome and disagree on the instrument, which is the clearest result this pipeline can produce. The UK issues no per-programme rating and reaches 'any time' by finding nothing for the watershed to bite on (UK-LAW-001, UK-SCH-002); France issues a real per-programme category and reaches the same hours by placing the programme in category I, which carries no clock restriction and no pictogram (FR-CLS-001). The divergence that would matter is one notch up: a French classification of II would keep the hours open but switch on the pictogram and written-mention obligations (FR-SIG-001, FR-SIG-002) and the children's-programming placement bar (FR-SCH-001), while the UK answer at that level would be unchanged. In the other direction the UK is the stricter of the two on the alcohol observation, because UK-DRG-001 addresses alcohol expressly before the watershed while the French slice contains no alcohol-specific rule and handles it only through the classification threshold. Both countries are decided on bright_line or conditional rules only, so neither is routed to a person; in both, the absent broadcast date is recorded as missing without changing the result, because the rules it feeds (UK-SCH-010, UK-SCH-011, FR-SCH-004) all operate on content tiers this programme does not reach.
